topic: Customers avoid phone calls but still want the work. Text is not a downgrade.

slides.subtitle: (they still want the job done)
slides.scene: Two phones lying side by side on a scuffed workbench, one dark and one showing a plain pale blue rectangle, a coil of copper pipe and a tape measure nearby in warm side light. All vehicles, buildings, doors and surfaces in shot have COMPLETELY BLANK panels with absolutely no writing, no company name, no logo, no lettering, no phone number and no graphics of any kind. No signage anywhere in the scene. There is NO text, no words, no numbers and no labels anywhere in the image.

caption:
Did you know a lot of your customers would rather text you than talk to you?

This one annoys people, because the phone has always worked. But a whole group of homeowners will not ring a stranger if there is any other option. They will fill in a form, send a message, or move on to a business that lets them.

It is not that they are less serious. Somebody who texts you at half nine at night about a leak is exactly as motivated as somebody who rings. They are just not going to have a conversation about it first.

So the question is not whether you like texting. It is whether a customer who will not ring can still reach you and end up booked.

Most contractors have no answer to that, and never find out what it cost them.
